0.label: Agent
0.summary: An autonomous AI system that reasons over objectives, breaks goals into sequential steps, and interacts with tools and environments to complete tasks.
0.plain_descriptions: an AI system that plans steps and uses tools to achieve goals independently a software assistant that observes its environment, takes actions, and completes tasks

1.label: Application Programming Interface (API)
1.summary: A set of defined rules, protocols, and endpoints enabling different software applications to communicate and exchange data.
1.plain_descriptions: a defined bridge that allows two software systems to talk to each other a digital waiter taking requests from one application to another

2.label: Endpoint
2.summary: A dedicated network address and URL path exposed by an API where clients access a specific service or resource.
2.plain_descriptions: the specific web address where an app sends requests to get certain information a digital front door where external software asks a server to do something

3.label: Cache
3.summary: A high-speed data storage layer that stores a subset of transient data so future requests are served faster than accessing primary storage.
3.plain_descriptions: a fast temporary storage area saving frequent answers so the computer skips slow re-calculations keeping copies of popular web pages in memory so users don't wait for slow database queries

4.label: CI/CD
4.summary: A modern engineering methodology uniting frequent source integration with automated regression testing and reliable application deployment.
4.plain_descriptions: automatically building, testing, and shipping code changes whenever engineers push work the automated pipeline that moves software from development to live production servers

5.label: Code review
5.summary: A collaborative peer-review practice where software engineers systematically examine proposed code changes to identify defects, enforce architectural standards, and share knowledge.
5.plain_descriptions: having teammate developers examine your code changes before merging a peer inspection of source code to catch bugs and uphold standards

6.label: Compound Interest
6.summary: Interest calculated on both the initial principal and the accumulated interest from previous periods.
6.plain_descriptions: interest on interest money snowballing because earnings get added back to the pile

7.label: Context window
7.summary: The maximum amount of text, counted in tokens, that a model considers in one request, covering the prompt, the conversation so far and its reply.
7.plain_descriptions: how much text the AI can keep in mind at once the AI’s working memory limit

8.label: Cookie
8.summary: A small piece of data stored on the user's browser by websites to retain state and track browsing activity.
8.plain_descriptions: small browser file websites save to remember your login web tracker banner you click accept on

9.label: Daily active users (DAU)
9.summary: The total count of unique individuals who initiate a meaningful interaction with a software application within a 24-hour day.
9.plain_descriptions: count of unique people who open and interact with an application in a single day vital metric tracking daily user volume and ongoing product engagement

10.label: Daily Scrum
10.summary: A 15-minute daily inspect-and-adapt event for developers to synchronize activities and plan the next 24 hours of work.
10.plain_descriptions: quick fifteen-minute daily morning meeting for developers to sync on sprint progress brief stand-up check-in where teammates share achievements, plans, and immediate blockers

11.label: Dataset
11.summary: A structured collection of data records, features, and targets partitioned to train, validate, and benchmark algorithms.
11.plain_descriptions: a structured collection of examples used to teach or test AI the organized data gathered together for machine learning experiments

12.label: Deep learning
12.summary: A specialized subset of machine learning utilizing multi-layered neural networks to extract hierarchical feature representations directly from complex data.
12.plain_descriptions: machine learning powered by deep neural networks with many hidden layers advanced AI techniques that automatically learn rich representations from raw data

13.label: Domain Name System (DNS)
13.summary: The hierarchical, decentralized naming system that translates human-readable domain names into numerical IP addresses for network routing.
13.plain_descriptions: the internet phonebook that translates human-friendly website names like example.com into computer IP addresses the directory service connecting domain names to web server numbers

14.label: Docker
14.summary: An open commercial platform providing tooling to build, share, package, and execute application containers using host operating system virtualization.
14.plain_descriptions: the most popular software tool for building, running, and managing containers the platform that popularised container packaging for modern software development

15.label: Encryption
15.summary: The cryptographic process of encoding plaintext into ciphertext so that only authorized parties with the matching decryption key can read it.
15.plain_descriptions: scrambling secret information into unreadable code that only someone with the correct key can unlock locking confidential data with a digital key so eavesdroppers see only scrambled nonsense

16.label: Environment variable
16.summary: A dynamic key-value pair stored in the operating system environment that configures program behavior without altering application source code.
16.plain_descriptions: a dynamic key-value setting stored outside software code to configure how it behaves in different environments a configuration variable provided by the operating system to running programs

17.label: Branch
17.summary: A lightweight movable reference pointing to a specific commit within a Git repository that represents an independent timeline of development.
17.plain_descriptions: an independent line of work in a repository allowing safe experimentation a movable pointer pointing to the latest commit in an isolated development path

18.label: Commit
18.summary: An immutable snapshot of staged changes recorded into Git repository history, associated with author metadata, timestamp, parent hashes, and a descriptive log message.
18.plain_descriptions: a saved snapshot recording the exact state of project files with an explanatory note a permanent record in the repository history describing what was changed and who changed it

19.label: Graphics Processing Unit (GPU)
19.summary: A specialized electronic processor optimized for high-throughput parallel execution of mathematical matrix operations essential for deep learning.
19.plain_descriptions: high-performance computer chips designed to handle massive parallel math for AI the dedicated hardware processors that accelerate neural network training and inference

20.label: Hallucination
20.summary: Output from a generative model that sounds plausible but is false or unsupported, presented as if it were fact.
20.plain_descriptions: when the AI confidently makes things up a made-up fact or fake citation from a chatbot

21.label: HTTP status code
21.summary: A standardized three-digit integer returned by a server indicating the outcome of a client’s HTTP request.
21.plain_descriptions: three-digit numbers that explain whether a web request succeeded or what went wrong the server’s quick status signal like 404 not found or 200 ok

22.label: Incident
22.summary: An unplanned interruption, degradation, or disruption of an IT service that impairs business operations or user experience.
22.plain_descriptions: an unplanned event that breaks software or degrades service quality for users a sudden technical emergency that requires immediate engineering intervention

23.label: Inference
23.summary: The operational stage where a trained model processes live inputs to generate predictions, decisions, or outputs without updating its parameters.
23.plain_descriptions: running a trained AI model to get live answers or classifications using an existing model on new inputs without changing its weights

24.label: Interest Rate
24.summary: The proportion of an amount loaned which a lender charges as interest to the borrower, typically expressed as an annual percentage.
24.plain_descriptions: percentage fee charged for borrowing money percentage reward earned on savings per year

25.label: JSON
25.summary: A lightweight, text-based data interchange format built on key-value pairs and ordered lists that is easy for humans to read and machines to parse.
25.plain_descriptions: a universal text format used to send data between websites and servers human-readable curly-brace text organizing names and values in software

26.label: Kanban
26.summary: A visual workflow management method designed to optimize continuous flow, limit work in progress, and maximize efficiency.
26.plain_descriptions: visual project management board that tracks work across columns and limits tasks in progress continuous delivery system focused on smoothing workflow and eliminating production bottlenecks

27.label: Key Performance Indicator (KPI)
27.summary: A quantifiable metric tracking ongoing operational efficacy and business performance against strategic benchmarks.
27.plain_descriptions: measurable target tracking whether a company or team is meeting its core operational goals key business metric showing the ongoing performance and financial health of a product

28.label: Linter
28.summary: A static code analysis tool that inspects source code for programmatic errors, stylistic inconsistencies, security antipatterns, and non-standard syntax before runtime.
28.plain_descriptions: a tool that scans your code to find style errors, suspicious patterns, and potential bugs an automated spell-checker for programming languages

29.label: Large Language Model
29.summary: A very large neural network trained on huge amounts of text that reads and writes language by predicting the next token.
29.plain_descriptions: an AI that writes text by guessing the next word the kind of chatbot brain behind ChatGPT, Gemini or Claude

30.label: Log
30.summary: A timestamped, discrete record of an event or state change emitted by a running computer program or system service.
30.plain_descriptions: a timestamped text record written by software to explain what it just did the running diary of events, errors, and actions that an application keeps

31.label: Machine learning
31.summary: A branch of artificial intelligence where computer systems detect underlying patterns in data to improve task performance without static rule engines.
31.plain_descriptions: software that learns rules from examples instead of explicit programming computer systems improving their accuracy automatically through experience

32.label: Multi-factor authentication (MFA)
32.summary: An authentication security method requiring users to supply two or more distinct evidence factors before granting access to a digital system.
32.plain_descriptions: logging in with two different proofs such as your password plus a code sent to your phone a security checkpoint requiring a password and a fingerprint before opening an account

33.label: Model
33.summary: A mathematical representation trained on data that captures patterns to generate predictions, decisions, or new content.
33.plain_descriptions: the trained software artifact that makes AI predictions an algorithm packed with learned weights ready to run

34.label: Training
34.summary: The iterative computational process of calculating errors and adjusting model weights against training data to minimize loss.
34.plain_descriptions: the computational process of teaching an AI model using data feeding examples into an algorithm so it can adjust its internal weights

35.label: Minimum Viable Product (MVP)
35.summary: An early iteration of a product incorporating the minimum feature set necessary to validate foundational assumptions with real customers.
35.plain_descriptions: simplest early version of a product built with just enough features to test with real users functional initial release designed to validate core business hypotheses with minimal engineering effort

36.label: Neural network
36.summary: A computational architecture comprising interconnected layers of artificial nodes that pass weighted signals through non-linear activation functions.
36.plain_descriptions: an AI computing structure inspired by interconnected biological brain cells layered mathematical nodes passing signals forward to identify complex patterns

37.label: Objectives and Key Results (OKR)
37.summary: A collaborative goal-setting framework pairing ambitious qualitative objectives with measurable key results to track organizational progress.
37.plain_descriptions: goal-setting system that pairs an inspiring objective with measurable numerical results quarterly framework aligning company direction, team focus, and quantifiable targets

38.label: Overfitting
38.summary: A modeling pathology where an algorithm learns idiosyncratic noise in training samples, severely impairing its ability to generalize to unseen data.
38.plain_descriptions: when an AI memorizes practice data so closely that it fails on fresh inputs an AI model scoring near perfect in practice tests but failing real exams

39.label: Principal
39.summary: The original sum of money lent, invested, or borrowed before interest accrues.
39.plain_descriptions: original sum of money borrowed or invested money before any interest gets calculated

40.label: Product backlog
40.summary: An evolving, ordered catalog of features, enhancements, and fixes representing the single source of work for a product team.
40.plain_descriptions: prioritized master list of features, bug fixes, and technical tasks waiting to be built single authoritative repository of planned work for the entire software product team

41.label: Product owner (PO)
41.summary: The Scrum role accountable for maximizing product value and managing the prioritized content of the product backlog.
41.plain_descriptions: person responsible for deciding what features a product should have and setting their priority key team member who connects user needs and business goals with development work

42.label: Product roadmap
42.summary: A strategic, evolving visual document mapping the vision, overarching direction, and planned milestones of a product over time.
42.plain_descriptions: high-level strategic timeline communicating where a product is heading and why visual guide that aligns executives, developers, and customers on major product milestones

43.label: Prompt
43.summary: The text, and sometimes images or files, given to a language model as input to steer what it produces.
43.plain_descriptions: what you type to tell the AI what to do the question or instructions you give a chatbot

44.label: Pull request (PR)
44.summary: A mechanism in distributed version control platforms that allows a developer to propose changes from a feature branch and request peer review before merging.
44.plain_descriptions: a formal request asking teammates to review and merge your branch into the main codebase a shared discussion page displaying proposed code changes in version control

45.label: REST
45.summary: An architectural style for network applications that uses standard HTTP methods to manipulate resources identified by URIs.
45.plain_descriptions: standard rules for how websites and apps exchange data over the web the way modern apps talk to servers using standard web addresses

46.label: Return on Investment
46.summary: A performance metric used to evaluate the efficiency or profitability of an investment relative to its cost.
46.plain_descriptions: how much money you make back compared to what you spent performance metric measuring profitability of an expense

47.label: Scrum
47.summary: A lightweight process framework structured around transparency, inspection, and adaptation to build products incrementally.
47.plain_descriptions: collaborative framework for developing complex products in short timeboxed iterations structured agile method featuring specific roles, backlogs, and iterative review meetings

48.label: Scrum master
48.summary: The Scrum role accountable for establishing Scrum practices, promoting team effectiveness, and removing operational impediments.
48.plain_descriptions: coach who guides the team in agile practices and removes blockers that slow down development facilitator who protects engineers from external distractions and improves team collaboration

49.label: Software Development Kit (SDK)
49.summary: A comprehensive collection of development tools, client libraries, documentation, and code samples designed for creating applications on a specific platform or service.
49.plain_descriptions: an all-in-one toolbox for building software for a specific platform a prepackaged set of tools and code libraries provided to developers

50.label: Semantic versioning
50.summary: A formal versioning specification utilizing a three-part numbering format (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH) to communicate the compatibility nature of software changes.
50.plain_descriptions: a three-part version numbering system showing whether updates contain fixes, new features, or breaking changes a standard release labeling scheme formatted as MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH to signal compatibility

51.label: Simple Interest
51.summary: Interest calculated exclusively on the original principal amount for the entirety of the loan or deposit period.
51.plain_descriptions: interest calculated solely on the initial deposit fixed interest payment that never compounds

52.label: Container
52.summary: A standard unit of software packaging code and all runtime dependencies to execute reliably in isolation on a shared OS kernel.
52.plain_descriptions: a lightweight sandbox containing an app and its dependencies to run anywhere reliably an isolated environment running software using shared operating system resources

53.label: Library
53.summary: A packaged collection of pre-written functions, classes, and subroutines that developers import and call directly to accomplish specific programmatic tasks.
53.plain_descriptions: a collection of reusable code routines that your program calls when needed a package of pre-written functions you import to perform specific tasks

54.label: Sprint
54.summary: A timeboxed iteration of one month or less during which a team builds a functional, verified product increment.
54.plain_descriptions: fixed development timebox usually running two weeks to build working features regular repeating cycle where a team converts selected backlog tasks into finished software

55.label: Sprint planning
55.summary: The collaborative event initiating each sprint where the Scrum team defines the sprint goal and forecasts backlog delivery.
55.plain_descriptions: collaborative meeting held at the start of a sprint to decide what work to tackle next planning session where the team establishes a sprint goal and selects backlog items

56.label: Sprint retrospective
56.summary: The final event of a sprint where the Scrum team inspects its past performance regarding people, relationships, process, and tools to identify actionable improvements.
56.plain_descriptions: end-of-sprint team meeting to review what went well and identify concrete ways to improve safe reflective space where teammates evaluate tools, processes, and interpersonal collaboration

57.label: SQL
57.summary: A standardized declarative programming language used to manage, query, and manipulate data stored in relational database management systems.
57.plain_descriptions: the standard computer language used to ask questions and edit data in relational databases the command language for reading, filtering, and inserting rows in tables like postgres or mysql

58.label: Stakeholder
58.summary: An individual, team, or organization that can affect, be affected by, or perceive itself to be affected by a product decision or outcome.
58.plain_descriptions: anyone who has an interest in, influences, or is affected by the outcome of a product key parties connected to a project, including end users, business leaders, investors, and regulatory bodies

59.label: Token
59.summary: Small chunk of text, typically subword units, processed by large language models.
59.plain_descriptions: unit AI uses to count text chunks why AI charges per prompt length

60.label: Unit test
60.summary: An automated test that isolates and verifies the behavioral correctness of the smallest testable component or function of an application.
60.plain_descriptions: an automated check testing the smallest single piece of code in isolation verifying that an individual function returns the correct answer for given inputs

61.label: Uptime
61.summary: The proportion or duration of time that a computer system, network, or application remains fully functional and accessible to users.
61.plain_descriptions: the percentage of time a computer system or website is running and ready for users how long a service stays available without crashing or going offline

62.label: User story
62.summary: A concise, non-technical explanation of a software requirement capturing user intent, desired functionality, and business value.
62.plain_descriptions: short informal description of a software feature framed from the perspective of an end user practical work item explaining who needs a capability, what they need, and why it provides value

63.label: Virtual machine (VM)
63.summary: A software emulation of a physical computer system that executes applications within a dedicated, isolated guest operating system managed by a hypervisor.
63.plain_descriptions: a software simulation of an entire physical computer running its own complete operating system a virtual computer created inside a powerful server that behaves just like a physical machine
